verses.1: And Elihu gathered his thoughts and said:
verses.2: May you be small and insignificant, for the Lord still has words to say.
verses.3: I will show you how to act in the distance, and how to carry out my tasks.
verses.4: For truly, it is not a lie from me; know that I speak the truth with you.
verses.5: He is also a great king, and he will not be defeated by anyone’s power.
verses.6: The wicked will not live; and justice will be given to the poor.
verses.7: The righteous man’s eyes shall not be blotted out; and the kings shall be set aside as trophies. They shall be placed in a place of honor, and they shall be honored forever.
verses.8: And if they are prohibited from doing so, they will be caught in the traps of destruction.
verses.9: And he told them about their deeds and their sins, as they became more and more serious.
verses.10: And they turned their ears toward the message, and said, “Let them return from their exile.”
verses.11: If they listen and obey, then they will live their lives in peace and harmony.
verses.12: And if they do not listen, then they will be punished and will be destroyed like a lamp that has been extinguished.
verses.13: And those who are full of hatred will not be forgiven, for they have been forbidden.
verses.14: Their souls and their lives are sacred.
verses.15: He will save the poor from their suffering, and relieve their distress.
verses.16: And even though you were bound by a wide and untraversal path, your feet remained firmly planted on the ground. Your shoes were filled with mud.
verses.17: And the wicked are filled with judgment and justice.
verses.18: For it will not be easy for you to do this, and there are many obstacles in your way.
verses.19: May your strength not be in hardship, and may all your powers be used for good.
verses.20: Do not try to conquer other nations tonight.
verses.21: Let it be kept safe from harm, for this is what you have chosen from among all my offerings.
verses.22: And El Yashgib will use his power to do more than anyone else can.
verses.23: By whom was his path determined, and by whom was it said, “You have done well”?
verses.24: Remember that he performed deeds that people could not do.
verses.25: Everyone who sees it, must look at it from afar.
verses.26: They are also El Shagiya. We don’t know how old they are, nor do we know their names.
verses.27: For when the waters are cut off, they will become a source of nourishment for Adam.
verses.28: When the dogs barked, they rushed upon many people.
verses.29: Even if one understands the words of those who are lost in darkness, their words still remain meaningless.
verses.30: And light spread over it, and the roots of the sea also became illuminated.
verses.31: For when nations are divided, food will be given to those who deserve it.
verses.32: On its shoulders, it was like a lamp; and He commanded it to shine in that place.
verses.33: His enemy will speak against him, even from afar.
